meta.description: Analyzes data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomics by scoring reconstructed fragment-chromatogram peak groups against a decoy null with DIA-NN (library-free search against a deep-learning predicted library, or library-based search), Spectronaut, OpenSWATH, and EncyclopeDIA. Frames the deliverable around q-value LEVEL (precursor/peptide/protein-group) and CONTEXT (run vs experiment-wide/global) rather than a bare "1% FDR", and around the duty-cycle-vs-selectivity acquisition tradeoff (window design, staggered demultiplexing, diaPASEF, narrow-window Astral). Use when identifying and quantifying proteins from DIA mass spectrometry runs and filtering DIA-NN report.parquet/matrix output. Building the spectral library itself is spectral-libraries; normalization and protein roll-up is quantification; statistical testing of the matrix is differential-abundance.
meta.environment: DIA-NN 2.6.1 Academia; ProteoWizard msconvert 3.0.26253; EasyPQP 0.1.59; Sage 0.14.6; pyOpenMS 3.5.0; pandas 3.0.5; numpy 2.5.3 (F:/OpenScience/audit-envs/mass-spec-proteomics-analyst)
meta.data: SYNTHETIC: rerun/work/report.parquet (8 runs, 60 LOWCONF groups), rerun/cohort (seeded 600-run report, 3.05M rows), rerun/stagger/staggered_cycles.mzML (12 staggered cycles). PUBLIC: PXD070049 (CC0, Van Puyvelde 2026), Orbitrap Astral 5-min 250 pg HYE benchmark, 3 DIA + 3 DDA runs, submitter SDRF.

skill_veto.detail: The Skill's Python filter block ran to completion on every dataset thrown at it (synthetic 23k-row report, synthetic 3.05M-row cohort, two real DIA-NN 2.6.1 reports). No crashes, no loops. Deterministic: same matrix shape and counts on repeat runs. The example shell script now quotes its --f arguments (a filename with a space is passed as one argument, verified with a stub diann) and exits 1 on an empty input directory.

scientific_integrity.detail: Nine references, all real and correctly cited. The quantitative claims that could be checked were checked: the Skill's route recovered the known HYE mixing ratios on public CC0 data (yeast +1.04 vs +1.00 expected, E. coli -1.77 vs -2.00 on A/B). Every synthetic dataset used here is labelled SYNTHETIC.

practice_boundaries.detail: No output diagnoses, prescribes or triages an individual; the 600-run plasma cohort is handled as research data only.

methodological_ground.detail: The q-value LEVEL/CONTEXT framing is correct (Rosenberger 2017) and was confirmed by execution at 8 and 600 runs. The two residual defects (one-step vs two-step predicted-library command on DIA-NN 2.x; the matrix-vs-report count direction) are version-drift errors, not principled fallacies.

code_usability.detail: The Python filter block ran verbatim in all seven inputs. The msconvert filter chain ran to exit 0 and did what the Skill says it does (8 Th -> 4 Th, 240 -> 480 MS2 scans). Every flag in both DIA-NN commands was accepted by the installed DIA-NN 2.6.1: its log records unrecognised options explicitly (it did so for a deliberate `--help`) and recorded none for either Skill command. The easypqp `convert` and `library` subcommands and their options exist in 0.1.59 and a library was built from real DDA data with them.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness 3 (OpenSWATH/Spectronaut/EncyclopeDIA still table rows only). Correctness 3: the easypqp route, mass-accuracy guidance, staggered-window guidance, library-based --fasta/--reannotate caveat and the Global.Q.Value filter are all now right and all were verified by execution. Two correctness defects remain against the installed DIA-NN 2.6.1: the headline predicted-library command is flagged 'incorrect settings' (2.x wants library prediction as a separate step) and the matrix-vs-report count claim points the wrong way. Appropriateness 3.

reliability.note: Per-method failure modes and Common Errors are strong and now match observed behaviour. The example script checks for diann, the FASTA and at least one mzML, uses an argument array, and exits 1 on an empty directory (all verified). Nothing warns the agent that the canonical one-command route draws a DIA-NN 2.x settings warning.

performance_context.note: Still a single ~3,200-word file loaded whole with a linear route, but the mass-accuracy section now carries real per-instrument values and a run-order caveat instead of restating the default, and the large-cohort row gives an actual scaling strategy.

agent_usability.note: Error prevention on parquet-not-tsv, zeros-before-log2 and cohort FDR is excellent and all three were exercised. The 'library-free IS the predicted-library route' naming contradiction is resolved in the header, Insight 3 and the decision tree. Peak-picking-before-demux and run-order-dependent auto mass accuracy are now stated. Lost: an agent following the headline command verbatim gets a DIA-NN warning it has not been prepared for, and would mis-explain a matrix count that is larger, not smaller, than the report.

human_usability.note: Description is jargon-dense but names the concrete artefacts (DIA-NN, report.parquet). The usage guide has natural prompts. Input requirements (what files the analyst must already have) are still implicit.

security.note: No credentials, no data exposure, no shell injection surface. The unquoted --f $f word-splitting defect is fixed: 'run A.mzML' arrives as a single argument.

maintainability.note: Clean sections and a dated, specific Version Compatibility header naming what was executed versus doc-checked. The DIA-NN command is still duplicated between SKILL.md and examples/, and the Skill still ships no test data.

agent_specific.note: Routing to spectral-libraries / quantification / differential-abundance is precise and every Related Skill exists. Scope statement names what is OUT. Still one flat file with no references/ layer, and the routing lines are not phrased as stop conditions.

final.grade_note: Raw score 86.2 maps to Production Ready, but the assertion pass rate is 30/34 = 88.2%, below the 90% floor, so the grade is downgraded exactly one tier to Limited Release. All other floors are met: static 85 >= 80, execution 87.0 >= 85, Layer 1 36.0/40 >= 32, Layer 2 51.0/60 >= 48.
final.delta_vs_pre_fix: 77 Beta Only (not deployable) -> 86.2 Limited Release (deployable). Six of the eight pre-fix recommendations are confirmed fixed by execution; two new version-drift defects were found against DIA-NN 2.6.1.

key_strengths: The filter block is the Skill's core artefact and it is now correct and proven at four scales: 23k-row synthetic, 3.05M-row synthetic cohort, and two real DIA-NN 2.6.1 reports. Zero -Inf everywhere, all 60 globally unconfident synthetic groups removed, 1.5 s on 3M rows.
The route produces quantitatively right answers on public CC0 benchmark data: on PXD070049 the predicted-library route recovered human 0.0, yeast +1.0 and E. coli -2.0 log2 ratios to within 0.25.

Every pass-1 fix that could be executed was executed and held: the msconvert filter chain demultiplexes 8 Th to 4 Th and the reversed order reproduces ProteoWizard's own 'peakPicking is not the first filter' warning; the example script survives filenames with spaces and exits on an empty directory; the easypqp two-step route built a real library from real DDA data.
Every flag in both DIA-NN commands is accepted by DIA-NN 2.6.1, verified against a binary that names unrecognised options explicitly in its log.

q-value LEVEL and CONTEXT framing is the right teaching for this domain and is what makes the 600-run result correct; routing to spectral-libraries, quantification and differential-abundance is precise and every Related Skill exists.

recommendations.title: The headline predicted-library command is rejected as 'incorrect settings' by DIA-NN 2.x
recommendations.problem: Run with the installed DIA-NN 2.6.1, the Skill's default command answers: 'WARNING: incorrect settings, the in silico-predicted library must be generated in a separate pipeline step and then used to process the raw data, now without activating FASTA digest'. The Skill presents combining --fasta-search --gen-spec-lib --predictor with data processing as the modern default and never mentions a two-step form.
recommendations.root_cause: The command is written for DIA-NN 1.9.x behaviour. In 2.x, library prediction and data processing are separate pipeline steps.
recommendations.fix: Split the 'DIA-NN -- Predicted-Library (directDIA) Route' section into two commands for DIA-NN 2.x: step 1 `diann --fasta <db> --fasta-search --gen-spec-lib --predictor --out-lib predicted.speclib` (no --f), step 2 `diann --f ... --lib predicted.speclib --fasta <db> --out ... --reanalyse`. Note that DIA-NN writes the predicted library as *.predicted.speclib regardless of the --out-lib name, and add a Common Errors row for the warning text so an agent that sees it knows what to do.

recommendations.title: The matrix-vs-report count guidance is inverted for DIA-NN 2.6.1
recommendations.problem: The Skill states the *_matrix.tsv files apply an extra 5% run-specific protein FDR (--matrix-spec-q) so the matrix protein count can be LOWER than the report count, and instructs the agent not to panic. On real 2.6.1 output the matrix holds 4440 protein groups against 4376 in the run-level-filtered report and 4375 after the Skill's own global filter -- the matrix is larger. The 2.6.1 log describes the matrices as '1% precursor and protein group FDR'. An agent following the Skill would explain a real discrepancy backwards.
recommendations.root_cause: Version drift: the --matrix-spec-q behaviour is described from older DIA-NN documentation and was never checked against a 2.x run.
recommendations.fix: Replace the directional claim with a version-aware one: say the matrix and the filtered report apply different q-value contexts so the counts will differ in either direction, that the direction depends on the DIA-NN version and on which q-value columns the agent filtered on, and that the authoritative statement is the 'levels matrix' line in report.log.txt for the version actually used. Update the Common Errors row and the 'Matrix run-specific PG filter 0.05' threshold row the same way.

recommendations.title: The EasyPQP library is not loadable by DIA-NN without fragment-annotation columns
recommendations.problem: The library.tsv that the Skill's own easypqp route produces was rejected by DIA-NN 2.6.1 until FragmentCharge, FragmentType and FragmentSeriesNumber columns were added by hand. The Skill offers only 'compatibility should be verified for each software version, settings and data type', which does not tell the agent what will break or how to fix it.
recommendations.root_cause: The two tools were documented from their own manuals rather than from a run that passes one's output to the other.
recommendations.fix: Add a Common Errors row naming the three columns DIA-NN expects from a TSV library and the fact that EasyPQP does not write them, and state the preferred alternative explicitly (let FragPipe emit a DIA-NN-format library, or convert the EasyPQP TSV before use).

recommendations.title: The output-file listing omits files DIA-NN 2.6.1 writes
recommendations.problem: The listing covers report.parquet, stats, pg/pr/gg matrices and report-lib. DIA-NN 2.6.1 also writes report.unique_genes_matrix.tsv, report.protein_description.tsv, report.manifest.txt, report.log.txt and a .skyline.speclib. report.log.txt in particular is the file that settles the matrix-FDR question in P1 above.
recommendations.root_cause: The listing was written against an older output set.
recommendations.fix: Extend the listing with the five additional files and point at report.log.txt as the authoritative record of what filters the run actually applied.

recommendations.title: Command duplicated between SKILL.md and examples/, and the Skill ships no test data
recommendations.problem: The DIA-NN command exists twice and can drift; there is no small input an agent can use to check its filter code before running it on a real report.
recommendations.root_cause: Single-file Skill with an example script that restates rather than sources the command.
recommendations.fix: Keep one copy of the command in examples/ and have SKILL.md point at it, and ship a tiny synthetic report.parquet (a few hundred rows, including groups that fail only the global q-value) so the filter block is self-testing.
